note: Every rule cites a receipt verified at a primary venue this session. See references/evidence.html. Tiers: 1=hard/deterministic, 2=conditional, 3=opinion/suggestion, 4=anti-folklore.

rules.claim: A color ramp stepped evenly in HSL/RGB is perceptually UNEVEN; perceptual evenness requires even steps in OKLab lightness.

receipt.source: MacAdam, 'Visual Sensitivities to Color Differences in Daylight'
receipt.chain: MacAdam proved color space is perceptually non-uniform (25,000 color-match trials) -> OKLab (Ottosson 2020) is engineered so equal numeric steps ~ equal perceived steps.

rules.fix: Regenerate the ramp with even OKLab-L steps (use oklch() with evenly-spaced L). Do not step HSL lightness evenly.

rules.claim: Body text must meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (>= 4.5:1 normal, >= 3:1 large) against its background.

receipt.caveat: WCAG 2.1 uses relative-luminance ratio; APCA / WCAG 3 (draft) model perceived contrast better for some cases. Ratio is the enforceable standard today.

rules.fix: Darken/lighten the foreground or background until the ratio meets AA. Avoid gray text on colored backgrounds; use a tint of the background hue instead.

rules.claim: Interactive targets below ~44x44px (iOS) / 48x48dp (Android) raise acquisition time and error rate; per Fitts's Law, smaller target width => longer, error-prone acquisition.

receipt.source: Fitts, 'The information capacity of the human motor system in controlling the amplitude of movement'
receipt.caveat: 44px/48dp are platform GUIDELINES (Apple HIG / Material) engineered around Fitts, not measured constants themselves.

rules.fix: Increase the tap target to >= 44px (extend hit area with padding if the visual must stay small). Place frequent targets closer / at screen edges (infinite-depth) to cut travel distance.

rules.claim: A type scale should follow a consistent ratio (e.g. 1.2 minor-third, 1.25, 1.333, 1.5); arbitrary near-duplicate sizes read as noise and weaken hierarchy.

receipt.source: Modular scale is design convention (Bringhurst, 'The Elements of Typographic Style'), NOT a human-measurement.
receipt.note: Labeled Tier-1 for CONSISTENCY-checkability, but the RATIO CHOICE is aesthetic tradition, not measured. Flagged honestly.

check.predicate: adjacent font-size ratios cluster around one constant (cv < 0.15)

rules.fix: Collapse near-duplicate sizes; pick one ratio and derive the scale from it. Cap distinct text sizes (~3-5) to keep hierarchy legible.

rules.claim: Do not force users to hold information in working memory across steps/screens; capacity is ~4 chunks, not 7.

receipt.source: Cowan, 'The magical number 4 in short-term memory: a reconsideration of mental storage capacity'
receipt.note: Supersedes Miller 1956's '7+-2', which was serial recall of unidimensional stimuli, not UI chunking.

check.predicate: Does any flow require the user to remember a value shown on a prior step to complete a later one? If yes, flag.

rules.fix: Carry the needed value forward on-screen (show the cart total, echo the entered code). Never make the user remember it.

rules.claim: Encode the primary quantitative comparison using position/length, not angle/area/color; humans decode position most accurately.

receipt.source: Cleveland & McGill, 'Graphical Perception: Theory, Experimentation, and Application to the Development of Graphical Methods'
receipt.note: Foundational ranked experiment; replicated on Mechanical Turk by Heer & Bostock (CHI 2010).

check.predicate: Is the key comparison encoded as a pie/donut (angle) or bubble (area) when a bar (length/position) would serve? If yes, flag.

rules.fix: Prefer bar/dot/line (position, length) for the main comparison. Reserve angle/area for secondary or part-of-whole framing only.

rules.claim: A bar chart of a mean cannot show the underlying distribution; many different distributions produce the identical bar. For small-n, show the data (dots/box).

receipt.source: Weissgerber et al., 'Beyond Bar and Line Graphs: Time for a New Data Presentation Paradigm'

check.predicate: Is a bar/line of a mean (with SE/SD) used to summarize a small continuous sample? If yes, suggest a distribution-revealing plot.

rules.fix: Use a univariate scatter/dot plot or box plot for small samples so outliers, bimodality, and n are visible.

rules.claim: FOLKLORE: 'limit UI elements/menu items to 7 (+-2) because of Miller's law.' Miller 1956 was serial recall of unidimensional stimuli, NOT visual-UI chunking; the real WM figure is ~4 (Cowan 2001). Do not cap layout by 7.

receipt.source: Miller 1956 (Psychological Review) misapplied; corrected by Cowan 2001 (Behavioral & Brain Sciences 24:87)

check.predicate: source text mentions 'magical number seven' / '7 plus or minus 2' / 'max 7 items' as a design justification

rules.fix: Drop the 7-item justification. Group by meaning (chunking) and reduce cross-step memory load; there is no scientific '7 widgets' cap.

rules.claim: FOLKLORE: 'lay out dashboards to follow the F-pattern.' NN/g's own eye-tracking says the F-pattern is the DEFAULT when there are no strong cues, is bad for users, and should be COUNTERACTED with hierarchy, not emulated.

receipt.source: Nielsen Norman Group, 'F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web' (eye-tracking, ~45-47 users/example)
receipt.note: Verified at source: NN/g recommends counteracting, not designing for, the F-pattern.

check.predicate: source text advocates 'design for the F-pattern' / 'follow the F-pattern' as a layout goal

rules.fix: Design deliberate visual hierarchy (headings, grouping, emphasis) so the eye is GUIDED. The F-pattern emerging is a symptom of missing hierarchy.

rules.claim: OVERSTATED: 'always maximize data-ink / erase all chartjunk' (Tufte). The strong form is empirically contested: Bateman 2010 found embellished charts were no worse for comprehension and BETTER for long-term recall. Treat as taste, not law.

receipt.source: Bateman et al., 'Useful Junk? The Effects of Visual Embellishment on Comprehension and Memorability of Charts'
receipt.note: Counterpoint to Tufte 1983's data-ink orthodoxy. Embellishment helped recall of title/theme, not specific values.

check.predicate: source text asserts 'maximize the data-ink ratio' or 'remove all chartjunk' as an absolute rule

rules.fix: Hold data-ink as a default aesthetic, not a law. Purposeful, topic-matched embellishment can aid memorability without hurting comprehension.

rules.claim: AI-DESIGN TELL: thick colored left/right border on cards/alerts/callouts. Overused signature of AI-generated admin/dashboard UIs.

receipt.source: Craft heuristic (impeccable detector, Bakaus). NOT a human-measurement — flagged as craft, tier-4.
receipt.note: Included honestly as craft, not science.

check.predicate: css declares border-left or border-right with width > 1px

rules.fix: Use a different structure to signal status (icon, background tint, heading) rather than a colored side stripe.

rules.claim: AI-DESIGN TELL: gradient-filled text (background-clip:text + gradient). Overused, hurts legibility.

receipt.source: Craft heuristic (impeccable detector, Bakaus). NOT science — craft, tier-4.

check.predicate: css combines background-clip:text (or -webkit-) with a gradient background

rules.fix: Use a solid text color. Reserve gradients for backgrounds/accents, not text fill.

rules.claim: AI-DESIGN TELL: 'Inter' (or bare system defaults) as the brand font. Every model trained on the same SaaS templates reaches for Inter; it reads as AI-generated. Choose a distinctive typeface deliberately.

receipt.source: Craft heuristic (impeccable, Bakaus — #1 listed AI font tell). NOT a human-measurement; craft, tier-4.

check.predicate: font stack or class references Inter as the primary UI font

rules.fix: Pick a distinctive typeface that fits the brand. If Inter is a deliberate choice for a specific reason, keep it — but decide, don't default.
